messages:
jorge: quick question — thinking about moving to per-signal pipelines in the agent to reduce gateway fanout and exporter load. anyone see major gotchas?

anika: +1 on reducing gateway load but per-signal in agent bumps resource use on edge hosts (disk + mem for buffers). also retention/TTL becomes trickier to enforce centrally.

maya: UX note: if we split pipelines per signal we need clear console mapping so teams can see trace/metric/log routes and per-route quotas. otherwise support burden spikes.

sam: agree with maya. also need metrics for exporter-retry/backpressure at the agent level so SRE can triage without jumping into customer infra.

ben: how are you thinking about exporter fanout? duplicate exporters per-signal will multiply egress cost unless we centralize some fanout in gateway.

jorge: prototype idea: agent holds light-weight pipelines for spans and metrics (low retention), forwards logs to gateway where we do richer processing & retention. reduces gateway CPU for spans.

anika: that's reasonable. we should standardize a policy for retention TTL override: agents have a per-signal max-ttl header enforced by gateway on ingress so customers can't route long-retention into low-cost buckets.

maya: can we represent that in the console as a "pipeline contract"? e.g., pipeline shows accepted TTL range, allowed exporters, and estimated egress cost. that would help customers pick right route.

sam: +1. also add a sampling knob surfaced in console per-tenant/per-route so they can trade quality for cost quickly.

ben: operational question: for rollouts, if we ship per-signal agent pipelines, we need an incremental toggle by tenant and fallback to gateway default. Otherwise a bad agent deploy can take down many tenants.

jorge: agreed. plan: canary config flag that flips pipeline mode for a tenant. fallback policy: if agent-side exporter fails, gateway should accept and continue pulling data for a short window.

collector-bot: CI check: recent agent-image builds have new pipeline templates at ops/collector/templates/per-signal.yaml.

jorge: dropping a quick snippet of the tentative agent config for spans (very rough):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
  memory_limiter:
    limit_mib: 512
exporters:
  redwood_span_exporter:
    endpoint: "+gateway:4317"
pipelines:
  traces:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
    exporters: [redwood_span_exporter]
```

anika: nit: add a small local span buffer path and a disk-queued-retry for flaky networks. otherwise agent restarts drop samples.

sam: and surface agent-side exporter-stats via /metrics so console can show per-tenant token-level cost estimates.

maya: action items: 1) eng-runtime spike to measure agent mem/disk cost for per-signal pipelines (jorge + anika). 2) console mockups for pipeline contract & sampling UX (maya + sam). 3) ops RFC on rollout/fallback semantics (ben).

ben: SGTM. can we land the spike in 2 weeks?

jorge: yes, will start tomorrow and post results in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
